outcome: No accepted proof or verified construction of a self-adjoint operator whose spectrum is the nontrivial zeros has appeared since 26 January 2024; the one in-window operator construction with a self-adjointness claim (Yakaboylu, arXiv 2408.15135, first posted 27 Aug 2024, latest version 18 Aug 2026) is unrefereed, its key similarity transformation is postulated in its body, and its self-adjointness rests on a positivity condition the paper itself says is equivalent to the Riemann hypothesis, while the 2026 AI-credited results (Anthropic on the proportion of zeros on the critical line; OpenAI on a zero-free half-plane) do not concern a self-adjoint operator.
problem_asks: (a) The existence of a self-adjoint operator H, on some Hilbert space with some specified domain. (b) The eigenvalues of H correspond to the nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function: each nontrivial zero gives an eigenvalue and each eigenvalue comes from a nontrivial zero. The statement does not fix the dictionary; the standard reading is rho = 1/2 + i*gamma with eigenvalue gamma (written here in plain text as ρ = 1/2 + iγ, eigenvalue γ). The statement is silent on multiplicities (whether a multiple zero gives a multiple eigenvalue) and on simplicity of zeros. Not separately asked, but a consequence under the standard dictionary: the Riemann hypothesis, because a self-adjoint operator has real spectrum. The bullet does not ask for a particular operator, a construction, or a proof of RH as such.

events.what_happened: Enderalp Yakaboylu, 'Hamiltonian for the Hilbert-Pólya Conjecture' (arXiv 2309.00405; published J. Phys. A: Math. Theor. 57, 235204, 2024). Proposes a candidate Hamiltonian with Dirichlet conditions whose eigenfunctions vanish at the nontrivial zeros, so its eigenvalues are said to correspond to those zeros; asserts a similarity transformation making it self-adjoint on a suitable domain; notes that if RH holds the eigenvalues are real and equal the imaginary parts of the zeros. First posted before the window; several revisions fall inside it.
events.revisions: v1 1 Sep 2023; v2 16 Nov 2023; v3 31 Jan 2024 (inside the window; text concedes the similarity transformation, and thereby the Hamiltonian, is not well-defined on the domain where the Berry-Keating Hamiltonian is self-adjoint and the boundary condition applies, citing Bellissard 2017); v4 22 Feb 2024; v5 14 May 2024; v6 21 Jun 2024. Journal: J. Phys. A 57 235204 (2024), DOI 10.1088/1751-8121/ad4c2d.
events.delivers: A candidate operator for which the zeros would be eigenvalues if RH holds, and a claimed similarity transformation that makes it self-adjoint on a domain. The v6 abstract frames the self-adjointness as an attempt ('In our attempt to demonstrate the latter'), and the v6 Discussion says 'the second stage requires further rigorous treatment'. Restricted to the Berry-Keating-type model; it does not establish an operator whose spectrum is all the nontrivial zeros.
events.remains: Problem_asks (a) and (b). The self-adjointness step is not rigorously established by the paper's own account, and the identification with all zeros is conditional on RH.
events.doubts: The v3 text (31 Jan 2024) concedes that the similarity transformation, and thereby the Hamiltonian, is not well-defined on the Berry-Keating domain (citing Bellissard 2017), as quoted from the arXiv HTML. The v6 Acknowledgements thank Michael Berry and Jean Bellissard 'for valuable discussions'; that is acknowledgement, not a check of the argument.
events.direction: Asserts the existence of the kind of operator the conjecture posits, but only for a candidate and conditionally; the self-adjointness step is presented as an attempt.
events.object: A candidate Hamiltonian (Berry-Keating type, Dirichlet conditions) whose eigenfunctions are said to vanish at the nontrivial zeros; a similarity transformation is claimed to make it self-adjoint on a restricted domain. The transformation is not shown to be well-defined on the Berry-Keating domain (concession in v3). Not explicit as a construction in the versions read.

events.what_happened: Yakaboylu posts a second paper on the same candidate: arXiv 2408.15135 v1 'On the Hamiltonian for the Hilbert-Pólya Conjecture' (27 Aug 2024). The v1 abstract says the eigenfunctions of the candidate are square-integrable and its eigenvalues are real, and calls this 'a significant step toward proving the Riemann Hypothesis'. The abstract does not claim an unconditional self-adjoint operator and does not mention a similarity transformation.
events.revisions: Full listing from the arXiv abstract page: v1 27 Aug 2024; v2 4 Sep 2024; v3 21 Sep 2024; v4 21 Oct 2024 (see yakaboylu-2408-v4-similarity-postulated); v5 1 Dec 2024; v6 13 Jan 2025; v7 20 Feb 2025; v8 11 Mar 2025; v9 23 Apr 2025 (see yakaboylu-2408-v9-existence); v10 12 Jun 2025; v11 27 Aug 2025; v12 2 Oct 2025; v13 18 Nov 2025 (see yakaboylu-2408-v13-positivity); v14 17 Dec 2025; v15 11 Mar 2026; v16 29 Jul 2026; v17 18 Aug 2026 (latest). Titles seen: v1 'On the Hamiltonian for the Hilbert-Pólya Conjecture'; v4 to v6 'Reality of the Eigenvalues of the Hilbert-Pólya Hamiltonian'; v9 to v11 'On the Existence of the Hilbert-Pólya Hamiltonian'; v13 and later 'Nontrivial Riemann Zeros as Spectrum'. Only v1, v4, v9, v13 and v17 were read directly; the rest are dates only.
events.delivers: Per the v1 abstract: the candidate's eigenfunctions are square-integrable and its eigenvalues are real. This is a claim about the 2023 candidate and does not assert a self-adjoint operator whose spectrum is the zeros.
events.remains: All of problem_asks: no self-adjoint operator is asserted in this version, and the reality claim is presented as a step toward RH.
events.doubts: The reality claim rests on the 2023 candidate, whose similarity transformation the 2023 v3 text concedes is not well-defined on the Berry-Keating domain (see yakaboylu-2023-hamiltonian). A 2026 outside critique (Feldmann, Dalhousie) addresses the later framework of this same arXiv record (see feldmann-2026-03-obstructions); it is not recorded as engaging v1 specifically.
events.direction: Supports the conjecture's direction only indirectly (reality of eigenvalues of a candidate), presented as progress toward RH rather than a resolution.
events.object: The 2023 candidate Hamiltonian; the v1 abstract claims its eigenfunctions are square-integrable and its eigenvalues real. No explicit operator with the full zero set.

events.what_happened: Version 4 of arXiv 2408.15135 (21 Oct 2024, titled 'Reality of the Eigenvalues of the Hilbert-Pólya Hamiltonian') asserts: 'We demonstrate the existence of a well-defined similarity transformation that renders this Hamiltonian self-adjoint for the nontrivial Riemann zeros.' Its body says: 'At this point, we postulate the existence of a similarity transformation that restricts the domain', 'Additionally, we assert that the transformed Hamiltonian is self-adjoint on this domain', and 'Rather than explicitly constructing the transformation, we seek to justify this postulate'. This is the first version I verified to carry the self-adjointness claim; v2 and v3 were not opened.
events.revisions: Part of the arXiv record 2408.15135 (see yakaboylu-2408-v1-reality for the full version list). v2 and v3 (4 and 21 Sep 2024) were not opened, so it is not established whether the self-adjointness claim first appeared there.
events.delivers: Per the abstract: existence of a similarity transformation making the Hamiltonian self-adjoint for the nontrivial zeros. Per the body: that existence is postulated and the transformed operator's self-adjointness on a domain fixed by the postulate is asserted. Establishes a conditional claim, not a constructed operator.
events.remains: Problem_asks (a): the transformation is not constructed and its domain is not justified in this version. Problem_asks (b): the identification with all zeros is not established.
events.doubts: The key transformation is postulated, not constructed, in the body (v4 text). The 2023 domain concession (Bellissard 2017) applies to the same construction. The 2026 Feldmann preprint (Dalhousie) argues the transformed Dirichlet domain is not dense in the Hilbert space, so the self-adjointness gap is ill-posed as formulated (from its abstract).
events.direction: Asserts the conjectured kind of operator exists for the nontrivial zeros, but with the existence postulated in the body; supports the direction conditionally.
events.object: A similarity transformation claimed to map the candidate Hamiltonian to a self-adjoint operator on a restricted domain. The transformation is not written down: the body says the author postulates it rather than constructing it. Not explicit.

events.what_happened: Version 9 of arXiv 2408.15135 (revised 23 Apr 2025, retitled 'On the Existence of the Hilbert-Pólya Hamiltonian') abstract: 'We present a construction of a self-adjoint Hamiltonian whose eigenvalues are of the form i(1/2 − ρ_s), where ρ_s denote the simple nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function.' It adds: 'Our results suggest that all nontrivial Riemann zeros are simple', and that 'Consequently, all such zeros lie on the critical line, marking a significant step toward a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis.'
events.revisions: Part of the arXiv record 2408.15135 (see yakaboylu-2408-v1-reality). v9 is dated 23 Apr 2025 on the arXiv listing; this version is the first in which I read the existence wording.
events.delivers: For the simple nontrivial zeros only: a claimed self-adjoint operator with eigenvalues i(1/2 − ρ_s); on the paper's own stated conclusion, these zeros would then lie on the critical line. Simplicity of all zeros is only suggested, not proved.
events.remains: Problem_asks (a) and (b) for all nontrivial zeros, including multiple zeros; and the simplicity of all zeros, which this version says is only suggested.
events.doubts: The self-adjointness is asserted for a construction whose key transformation was postulated in v4. The abstract frames simplicity as a suggestion. The later Feldmann preprint argues against the framework (see feldmann-2026-03-obstructions).
events.direction: Asserts the conjectured kind of operator exists for simple zeros; supports the direction, restricted to simple zeros.
events.object: A self-adjoint operator with eigenvalues i(1/2 − ρ_s) for the simple nontrivial zeros, presented as a construction. The later v11 abstract places it on L²[0,∞); that statement is not from v9 and was not verified there.

events.what_happened: Version 13 of arXiv 2408.15135 (18 Nov 2025, titled 'Nontrivial Riemann Zeros as Spectrum'). The v13 abstract says: 'We first show that the existence of a rank-one Riesz projector entails' a nonvanishing of ζ′ at each nontrivial zero, which the author treats as establishing simplicity; introduces a non-symmetric operator whose spectrum corresponds to the zeros; constructs a positive semidefinite intertwining operator W linked to Weil's positivity criterion, whose positivity 'enforces Re(ρ)=1/2 for all ρ, in accordance with the Riemann Hypothesis'; and says it constructs a self-adjoint Hilbert–Pólya operator whose spectrum coincides with the imaginary parts of the nontrivial zeros.
events.revisions: Part of the arXiv record 2408.15135. v13 18 Nov 2025; v14 17 Dec 2025; v15 11 Mar 2026; v16 29 Jul 2026; v17 18 Aug 2026 (latest). In v17 the main theorem is stated 'Assume that all nontrivial Riemann zeros are simple', and Section 4 says 'it is an open question whether all nontrivial Riemann zeros are simple'. The v15 change (simplicity assumed rather than shown) is from a search-snippet summary, not from opening v15.
events.delivers: Per the v13 abstract: a claimed self-adjoint Hilbert–Pólya operator with the zeros as spectrum, with a claimed proof of simplicity. The latest text (v17, Observation 4.7) says that 'the self-adjointness of ĥ rests on the positivity Ŵ > 0', and that this condition 'already entails ℜ(ρ)=1/2, and so embodies the content of the RH'. So the operator's existence is conditional on a condition the paper states is equivalent to RH; the paper does not show Ŵ > 0.
events.remains: Problem_asks (a), unconditionally: the positivity Ŵ > 0 is stated to be equivalent to RH and is not shown. Problem_asks (b) for multiple zeros. Simplicity is an assumption in v17, not a proved result.
events.doubts: (1) Self-adjointness is conditional on Ŵ > 0, which the paper says is equivalent to RH (v17 text). (2) v13 says simplicity is shown, while v17 says it is an open question and assumes it: a change of claim between versions that the record does not explain. (3) Feldmann's obstructions (2026) target this framework: non-dense transformed domain, conjugate pairs rather than reality, and an unbounded intertwiner whose domain excludes the eigenfunctions.
events.direction: Asserts existence of the conjectured kind of operator, supporting the direction, but conditional on a positivity condition the paper itself equates with RH.
events.object: A non-symmetric operator R whose spectrum is {i(1/2 − λ)} over the zeros of the completed function; a positive semidefinite intertwining operator W between the compressed operator and its adjoint; and a self-adjoint operator built from them. Self-adjointness depends on W > 0, which is not shown. Not explicit about the positivity.

events.what_happened: Nathan Feldmann (Dalhousie University), 'Obstructions to the Spectral Proof of the Riemann Hypothesis via the Yakaboylu Hamiltonian' (Zenodo preprint, 31 Mar 2026, CC BY 4.0). Identifies three obstructions to completing the Yakaboylu program: the transformed Dirichlet domain is not dense in the Hilbert space; the bounded positive intertwining operator gives only conjugate pairs of eigenvalues rather than reality; and the unbounded intertwining operator that would give reality has a domain that excludes the eigenfunctions. Argues that the completeness condition needed under pseudo-Hermitian operator theory is equivalent to the Nyman-Beurling criterion.
events.revisions: Zenodo record shows v1 only.
events.delivers: A critique: argues that the Yakaboylu construction (arXiv 2408.15135) has three obstructions and that its closing condition is equivalent to Nyman-Beurling. It establishes no spectrum for any operator and does not settle the problem.
events.remains: Problem_asks (a) and (b): this record addresses neither positively.
events.doubts: This is itself a critique on Zenodo, not peer reviewed. I read the Zenodo abstract summary, not the full PDF (the summary is the fetch tool's paraphrase with three quoted obstructions). I found no reply from Yakaboylu in the later versions I read (v16 and v17 do not mention it; v17 restates the positivity equivalence).
events.direction: Cuts against the Yakaboylu route as formulated; says nothing for or against the conjecture as such.

events.what_happened: Bridger Logan, Substack post 'The Zeta Resonator: A Machine That Proves the Riemann Hypothesis in Lean' (23 Apr 2025). Claims 'a complete Lean 4.2 formalization of a spectral approach to the Riemann Hypothesis', with an operator whose 'spectrum corresponds to the nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function', 'self-adjoint, defined on a rigorous domain', 'no sorry', and 'no assumptions of the Riemann Hypothesis'. States 'This project is not being submitted for review'. No repository link appeared in the fetched text.
events.delivers: As claimed by the post: a machine-checked self-adjoint operator with the zeros as spectrum, with no RH assumption. Not verified by me; no code was opened.
events.remains: Nothing verified. If the claim held, it would cover problem_asks (a) and (b).
events.doubts: A single-author blog post with no repository in the fetched text and an explicit note that it is not submitted for review. The fetched text gives the build status line as 'Fully compiling, no', which is unclear and may mean the project does not fully compile; I could not check the original layout to confirm.
events.direction: Claims the conjectured kind of operator exists, with a formal proof; claims no RH assumption.
events.object: A 'Zeta Resonator' operator described as self-adjoint on a rigorous domain with spectrum the nontrivial zeros; no explicit form in the fetched text.

events.what_happened: Antonios Valamontes, Ioannis Adamopoulos and Guma Ali, 'Spectral realization of the nontrivial zeros of the Riemann Zeta function via a Hermitian operator framework' (Babylonian Journal of Mathematics 2025, pp. 50–60; repository issue date 18 May 2025; repository record added 17 Dec 2025). Abstract: an operator H∞ on a discrete space modelled on a 20-vertex dodecahedral graph, combining a discrete Laplacian, an entropy-based potential and a prime-indexed infinite-order term; 'We show that H∞ is self-adjoint'; its spectrum 'coincides exactly with the imaginary parts of the nontrivial zeros'; the construction 'supports a spectral-theoretic resolution of the Riemann Hypothesis'.
events.revisions: None found. The date is the repository's issue date for the journal item; no earlier public posting was located, so this may be later than a first posting.
events.delivers: Per the abstract: a claimed self-adjoint operator on a finite-graph model whose spectrum equals the zeros; a truncated numerical approximation is reported. The abstract does not explain how the discrete model's spectrum relates to the zeta zeros beyond the stated Hadamard-product match.
events.remains: Problem_asks (a) and (b) pending expert verification of the self-adjointness and of the link from the discrete model to ζ.
events.directly_checkable: The 20-vertex dodecahedral model and its truncation are described in the abstract; the full text was not read.
events.doubts: The repository record gives no referee or editorial statement; the publisher (Mesopotamian Academic Press, ISSN 3006-113X) has its review process undocumented in what I read. 'Infinity Algebra', the source of the prime-indexed term, appears in no other source I found.
events.direction: Claims self-adjointness and an exact spectral match (supporting direction) for a discrete operator.
events.object: H∞ on a discrete space modelled on the 20-vertex dodecahedral graph, with a discrete Laplacian, an entropy-based coherence potential and a prime-indexed infinite-order term; its spectral determinant is claimed to match the Hadamard product for ζ(1/2 + it). The operator is explicit in the abstract; numerical checks on a truncation are reported.

events.what_happened: Xingpao Suo, 'Hamiltonian with Energy Levels Corresponding to Riemann Zeros' (arXiv 2505.21192, first posted 27 May 2025; Phys. Rev. A 112, L060201, 2025). Constructs a Hamiltonian whose eigenenergies are ρ_n(1 − ρ_n), generalising the Berry-Keating paradigm with modular forms. States 'Although our construction does not resolve the Hilbert-Pólya conjecture', because the eigenstates are not normalizable; offers a physical reformulation of RH.
events.revisions: v1 27 May 2025; v2 29 Jun 2025; v3 5 Aug 2025; v4 6 Aug 2025; v5 25 Dec 2025. Journal reference: Phys. Rev. A 112, L060201 (2025).
events.delivers: A Hamiltonian whose eigenenergies are ρ_n(1 − ρ_n), a different quantity from the ordinates γ_n. By the author's own statement it does not resolve the Hilbert-Pólya conjecture.
events.remains: Problem_asks (a) and (b): the author says the conjecture is not resolved.

checked_by.what_they_did: Published the article (Phys. Rev. A 112, L060201, 2025); the record does not describe the refereeing

events.direction: Does not prove the conjecture and says so; its eigenvalues are ρ(1 − ρ), so it is not an operator with the zeros as eigenvalues.
events.object: A Hamiltonian with eigenenergies ρ_n(1 − ρ_n), built with modular forms; its eigenstates are not normalizable, which is why the author says the Hilbert-Pólya conjecture is not resolved.

events.what_happened: Fabrizio Tamburini (Rotonium – Quantum Computing), 'A Majorana Relativistic Quantum Spectral Approach to the Riemann Hypothesis in (1+1)-Dimensional Rindler Spacetimes' (arXiv 2503.09644, first posted 12 Mar 2025). Claims an exact spectral realization of the nontrivial zeros via a Mellin-Barnes integral linked to a Majorana particle; says the Hamiltonian is Hermitian and essentially self-adjoint; states the spectral correspondence and self-adjointness 'imply that all nontrivial zeros have real part Re(z)=1/2'; closes by calling it 'a promising Hilbert-Pólya-inspired path to prove the Riemann Hypothesis'.
events.revisions: v1 12 Mar 2025; v2 17 Apr 2025; v3 22 Jul 2025 (corrected typos and formulae; added a toy example with the Dirichlet beta function, per the comments field).
events.delivers: Per the abstract: a claimed exact spectral realization of the zeros with essential self-adjointness, implying RH. Claimed, not verified; the abstract's closing sentence is more hedged than its middle, so the paper's own status is ambiguous.
events.remains: Problem_asks (a) and (b) pending verification of the essential self-adjointness and of the spectral identification.
events.doubts: Single author with a company affiliation and no journal reference. The abstract's RH implication is stated firmly, while the closing sentence calls the work a 'promising' path. I read the text to about 200k of 231k characters (Sections I to III.2.1); appendices and the end matter were not read.
events.direction: Claims the conjectured kind of operator exists and that it implies RH (supporting direction, as claimed).
events.object: A Hamiltonian linked to a Majorana particle in (1+1)-dimensional Rindler spacetime, whose eigenvalues are claimed to be the nontrivial zeros through a Mellin-Barnes integral. The construction is not explicit in the abstract.

events.what_happened: Alain Connes, Caterina Consani and Henri Moscovici, 'Zeta Spectral Triples' (arXiv 2511.22755, first posted 27 Nov 2025; to appear in an EMS Lecture Notes volume on noncommutative geometry applications, per the arXiv comments). Builds self-adjoint operators as rank-one perturbations of a spectral triple tied to the scaling operator on [λ⁻¹, λ], using Euler products over primes up to a cutoff; reports spectra matching the lowest zeros of ζ(1/2 + is). Abstract: 'Numerical experiments show that the spectra of the operators converge towards the zeros'; 'A rigorous proof of this convergence would establish the Riemann Hypothesis.' Section 8: 'There are two essential steps still missing to justify our tentative proof of the Riemann Hypothesis.'
events.revisions: v1 27 Nov 2025 only, per the arXiv listing.
events.delivers: Numerical evidence: finite-cutoff self-adjoint operators whose low-lying spectra approximate the lowest zeros. Convergence as the cutoff grows is not proved. Establishes no limit operator and no exact identification of the zeros as eigenvalues.
events.remains: Problem_asks (a) and (b) in the limit: convergence of the operators, the self-adjointness of any limit, and the exact spectral identification. The authors say two steps are missing.
events.directly_checkable: The finite-cutoff matrices and their spectra are checkable numerically; not run here.
events.doubts: The authors call the argument 'tentative' and say two essential steps are missing (Section 8). No public engagement with the paper was found in my searches.
events.direction: Numerical support for the conjecture's direction at finite cutoffs; no proof.
events.object: Finite-cutoff self-adjoint operators (rank-one perturbations of a spectral triple on [λ⁻¹, λ]) whose spectra match the lowest zeros numerically; not a limit operator.

events.what_happened: A. Ladjeroud, 'The existence of Hilbert-Pólya operator' (preprints.ru, DOI 10.24108/preprints-3113840; posted 4 Nov 2025). Abstract: 'Hilbert-Pólya conjecture is proved by constructing Hilbert-Pólya operator' and 'Hence, the Riemann hypothesis is true.' The site states the article is a preprint and has not been peer-reviewed.
events.revisions: Page shows version 1 dated 04.11.2025. A search snippet gives a PDF dated 1 Nov 2025; not reconciled.
events.delivers: Per the abstract: a self-adjoint operator with the imaginary parts of the critical-line zeros as eigenvalues, hence RH. The argument itself was not readable: the PDF returned binary through the fetch tool, so no step can be assessed here.
events.remains: Problem_asks (a) and (b) if the claim held; nothing verified.
events.doubts: The site itself says the article is an unreviewed preprint and that results in preprints should not be reported in the media as verified information. The argument was not readable in my fetch. Method details (an auxiliary operator, supersymmetric quantum mechanics, multivalued operators) come from a search snippet, not from the paper.
events.direction: Claims the conjecture and RH are proven; if correct, cuts for the conjecture.
events.object: A self-adjoint 'Hilbert-Pólya operator' whose eigenvalues are said to be the imaginary parts of the critical-line zeros; no explicit form read.

events.what_happened: Zeraoulia Rafik (with Pedro Caceres in v2), 'If our chaotic operator is derived correctly, then the Riemann hypothesis holds true' (arXiv 2404.00583, first posted 31 Mar 2024). The v2 abstract builds a discrete map and a self-adjoint 'chaotic' operator on a weighted Hilbert space, proves it is unbounded and essentially self-adjoint, and compares finite truncations with GUE statistics; it states the work is 'without attempting to prove the Riemann Hypothesis' and 'a concrete Hilbert–Pólya–type framework rather than a proof of the conjecture'.
events.revisions: v1 31 Mar 2024 (Zeraoulia alone; per a search snippet v1 said the operator 'strongly supports' the Hilbert-Pólya view; v1 not opened); v2 24 Dec 2025 (adds Caceres; disclaimer of an RH proof).
events.delivers: Per v2: an essentially self-adjoint operator on a weighted Hilbert space and numerical GUE-type truncations. The operator's spectrum is not identified with the zeros, and the paper claims no RH proof.
events.remains: Problem_asks (b): the identification of the spectrum with the zeros. Problem_asks (a) is for a chaotic operator rather than an operator with the zeros as spectrum.
events.doubts: The title is conditional ('if ... derived correctly'). Numerical GUE agreement is evidence, not proof, and the paper says so. The v2 comment names 'Pedro Ceras' while the author is 'Pedro Caceres', which may be a typo.
events.direction: A framework; it does not claim RH and does not identify the spectrum with the zeros.
events.object: A self-adjoint 'chaotic' operator on a weighted Hilbert space; its finite truncations' eigenvalue statistics agree numerically with GUE predictions. Not identified with the zeros.

events.what_happened: Alain Connes, 'The Riemann Hypothesis: Past, Present and a Letter Through Time' (arXiv 2602.04022, submitted 3 Feb 2026; the comments say it was submitted to the Journal of Open Mathematical Problems on 19 Sep 2025). A survey of RH approaches with a 'Letter to Riemann': a quadratic-form optimisation using primes below 13 gives 'remarkable approximations to the zeros of zeta' (the first 50), and 'Moreover we prove a general result that these approximating values lie exactly on the critical line'. Outlines a possible strategy based on convergence of zeros from finite to infinite Euler products, which it calls 'a promising direction for future research'.
events.revisions: v1 3 Feb 2026 only in the arXiv listing read. A search snippet of the journal page gives the journal issue (2(1), 2026) and acceptance dates; not opened.
events.delivers: Approximating values for finitely many zeros from a finite-prime truncation, with a general result that those approximating values lie on the critical line. The approximating values are not the zeros, and the paper establishes no self-adjoint operator with the zeros as spectrum.
events.remains: Problem_asks (a) and (b). The paper's own strategy (convergence from finite to infinite Euler products) is described as a direction, not a result.
events.doubts: The critical-line result concerns approximating values, not zeros. Passing to zeros needs the convergence step the paper calls a possible strategy.
events.direction: Does not resolve; the approximations are finite objects whose property does not transfer to zeros without further argument.
events.object: Approximations to the first 50 zeros from primes below 13 via a quadratic-form optimisation. Explicit approximations; no operator with the zeros as spectrum.

events.what_happened: Peter Jaksch, 'Successive generation of nontrivial Riemann zeros from a Wu-Sprung type potential' (arXiv 2510.16759, 19 Oct 2025). Numerical experiments produce a symmetric potential for a 1D Schrödinger equation whose eigenspectrum is said to match the imaginary parts of the first nontrivial zeros. The abstract does not state an operator theorem and does not mention Hilbert-Pólya or RH.
events.revisions: v1 only.
events.delivers: A numerical match between computed eigenvalues of a constructed potential and the first zeros. No theorem.
events.remains: Problem_asks (a) and (b) in full.
events.directly_checkable: The potential and its eigenvalues are stated numerically; not run here.
events.direction: Numerical support for the first zeros; no operator theorem.
events.object: A symmetric potential for a 1D Schrödinger equation whose numerically computed eigenvalues approximate the imaginary parts of the first nontrivial zeros.

events.what_happened: Antonio Bonelli (listed as Researcher; no institution on the record), 'The Exact Spectral Realization of the Riemann Zeta Function: A Geometric Proof of the Riemann Hypothesis via A_{k-1} Lattice Cohomology, Integer Partitions, and the Bonelli Operator' (Zenodo preprint, published 28 Mar 2026, modified 31 Mar 2026; the record notes a newer version exists). Abstract: 'We present a rigorous proof of the Riemann Hypothesis'; the zeros of these operators 'are strictly confined to the critical line'; 'definitively validating the Hilbert-Pólya conjecture'. The record is marked as derived from arXiv 2602.03162.
events.revisions: v1 28 Mar 2026; modified 31 Mar 2026; the Zenodo page says a newer version exists, which I did not locate.
events.delivers: Per the record: a self-adjoint operator from the spectral theory of geometric Laplacians, with zeros on the line; claims RH. Not verified.
events.remains: Problem_asks (a) and (b) pending any check of the self-adjointness and the spectral identification.
events.doubts: Self-published Zenodo record with no peer review statement. The arXiv paper it is 'derived from' (arXiv 2602.03162, 'The Kaleidoscopic Filter, Part I') is about integer partitions. Its abstract and the first ~100k characters of its HTML (abstract through Section 7.5) do not mention the Hilbert-Pólya conjecture or the Riemann hypothesis, so the stated derivation is not visible in what I read.
events.direction: Claims to prove RH and the conjecture; cuts for the conjecture if correct.
events.object: A 'Bonelli operator' built from A_{k-1} lattice cohomology and integer partitions, described as self-adjoint with zeros on the critical line; no explicit construction in the record.

events.what_happened: Antonio Bonelli (Università della Basilicata, per the record), 'Proof of the Hilbert-Pólya Conjecture: Integrating Integer Partitions, the Riemann Zeta Function, and the General Transform' (Zenodo preprint, published 6 Jun 2026, modified 7 Jun 2026; 'Related works': derived from arXiv 2602.03162 and DOI 10.5281/zenodo.19456765). Description: the zeros are 'exact spectral resonances' of a partition manifold; a self-adjoint Hamiltonian is constructed in a Gelfand rigged Hilbert space; 'This provides an unassailable proof of the Hilbert-Pólya conjecture'; all nontrivial zeros 'strictly lie on the critical line'.
events.revisions: v1 6 Jun 2026; modified 7 Jun 2026.
events.delivers: Per the record: a self-adjoint Hamiltonian in a rigged Hilbert space whose spectrum is the zeros, and RH. The record does not say how self-adjointness is defined in that rigged setting, which is not the plain Hilbert-space setting of problem_asks.
events.remains: Problem_asks (a) and (b) pending verification; the rigged-space self-adjointness is unexplained in the record.
events.doubts: Self-published, no peer review. The arXiv paper it cites as its source (arXiv 2602.03162) does not mention Hilbert-Pólya or RH in the text I read (see bonelli-2026-03-rigorous-rh). The record also lists claims (GUE statistics, Voronin universality) with no supporting detail in the record.
events.direction: Claims the conjecture is proved; cuts for the conjecture if correct.
events.object: A self-adjoint Hamiltonian in a Gelfand rigged Hilbert space, said to have the zeros as spectrum; not explicit in the record.

events.what_happened: Charles Tibedo (no affiliation on the record), 'The Hilbert–Pólya Generator: Resolving the Riemann Hypothesis through Cartan–Klein Spectral Determinants' (Zenodo computational notebook, published 1 Jul 2026, v1, CC BY 4.0). Subtitle: 'A Constructive Proof of the Riemann Hypothesis via Cartan-Klein Spectral Isomorphism'; says it 'Contains the formal proof of the Hilbert-Pólya conjecture'; 'We resolve the Hilbert-Pólya conjecture through the definition of a Cartan-Klein spectral attractor'; a sequence of finite matrices whose determinants converge to the completed xi function; a limit operator said to be self-adjoint; 'all nontrivial zeros ... are algebraically constrained to the critical line'. Cites a residual of about 2.5 × 10⁻³⁸⁶⁹ at N = 128.
events.revisions: v1 only.
events.delivers: Per the record: a self-adjoint limit operator for a sequence of finite matrices whose determinants converge to ξ, placing zeros on the line. The 'formal proof' is a set of Python and SymPy computational modules and run certificates, not a proof assistant development.
events.remains: Problem_asks (a) and (b), including the convergence and self-adjointness of the limit; nothing verified.
events.directly_checkable: The record lists a Python script (spectral_certificate_v13_grid_correct_final.py), a JSON run certificate and text files; not run here.
events.doubts: Self-published, no peer review. The record calls numerical certificates a 'formal proof' and a residual of 10⁻³⁸⁶⁹ 'supporting evidence'; the finite-N certificates do not by themselves establish convergence of the limit.
events.direction: Claims the conjecture and RH proven; cuts for the conjecture if correct.
events.object: A Cartan–Klein spectral attractor; finite matrices whose determinants are said to converge to ξ, and a claimed self-adjoint limit operator. Not explicit beyond the record's description.

events.what_happened: Dean Kulik, 'Operator-Theoretic and Computational Realizations of the Riemann Hypothesis Expanded' (Zenodo thesis-type record, published 3 Jul 2026, v1, CC BY-NC 4.0). Reports that for a prime-zeta round-trip operator the critical line 'is not a maximum for the spectral radius, but a strict, robust minimum', calling this 'a fatal structural flaw in this formulation'; describes an independent computational implementation of the Connes–van Suijlekom truncated Weil quadratic form (attributed to Akiva Groskin, May 2026; not opened); states 'The remaining mathematical frontier resides solely in formalizing the final analytic bound'.
events.revisions: v1 only (created 2 Jul 2026, published 3 Jul 2026).
events.delivers: A review plus computational work: it reports a flaw in one operator formulation (a negative result for that formulation). It does not explicitly claim a complete proof of RH, although it contains phrases such as 'definitively proving' and says the remaining frontier is formalising a bound.
events.remains: Problem_asks (a) and (b) for any operator whose self-adjointness and spectrum are established.
events.doubts: Self-published, no peer review. The record mixes a negative result about one formulation with language implying near-completion, and I cannot tell from the record which the author stands by. The Groskin campaign it describes was not opened.
events.direction: Mixed: reports a flaw against one formulation; the closing remarks suggest the author regards the remaining step as a bound. Neither settles problem_asks.

events.what_happened: Michael Aksman, 'A Fredholm–Scattering Program for the Hilbert–Pólya Operator' (Zenodo poster, v2; availability date 11 Aug 2026; Zenodo publication date 28 Aug 2026). Abstract: truncated quadratic forms on a non-compact arithmetic orbifold with a uniform coercivity bound; projection onto the continuous Eisenstein scattering subspace; a Mosco limit H∞ described as strictly self-adjoint with compact resolvent on that subspace; the Selberg trace formula links the scattering determinant to ξ(s); 'we prove that all spectral parameters γn must be purely real, thereby establishing the Riemann Hypothesis'.
events.revisions: v2 on Zenodo; v1 not located. The record lists availability on 11 Aug 2026 and publication on 28 Aug 2026; I used the earlier date.
events.delivers: Per the record: a self-adjoint limit operator whose spectrum is the zeros, and RH. Not verified; the record makes no statement of review.
events.remains: Problem_asks (a) and (b): self-adjointness of H∞ and identification of its spectrum with the zeros are the claimed steps; nothing checked.
events.doubts: Self-published poster with no peer review statement and no affiliation. I read the Zenodo record page only; the PDF was not read.
events.direction: Claims the conjecture and RH proven; cuts for the conjecture if correct.
events.object: A limit operator H∞ built from truncated quadratic forms on an arithmetic orbifold and projected onto the Eisenstein subspace; not explicit beyond the record's abstract.

events.what_happened: Kejun Liu (Soochow University), 'Metric completion of the Bender–Brody–Müller Hamiltonian: dilation spectrum and missing eigenstates' (arXiv 2607.19067, math-ph, submitted 21 Jul 2026). Shows that the metric completion of the BBM form is positive but not coercive; that the free self-adjoint realization is the dilation generator; that the BBM candidate functions are not in the completed space on Re z = 1/2; and concludes that 'the original BBM boundary-condition/eigenfunction mechanism cannot produce point-spectrum Riemann-zero states' in this completion. States the theorem 'rules out the original BBM candidate-eigenfunction/boundary-condition mechanism, not every construction inspired by it'. Cites Yakaboylu's J. Phys. A paper in passing without analysing it.
events.revisions: v1 only.
events.delivers: A negative result: the BBM candidate-eigenfunction mechanism does not produce Riemann-zero eigenstates in this L²-based metric completion. It explicitly does not resolve Hilbert-Pólya or RH, and does not rule out other constructions.
events.remains: Problem_asks (a) and (b) remain open, including for constructions 'inspired by' BBM.
events.direction: Negative for the BBM route only; the paper's own scope excludes a verdict on the conjecture.
events.object: No object for the conjecture: the paper shows the BBM candidate functions ψ_z are not in the completed space on Re z = 1/2.

events.what_happened: Anthropic's research post (published 10 Aug 2026; updated 13 Aug 2026) reports that 'An unreleased research version of Claude found the new lower bound over two sessions in Claude Code, using a total of 31 million output tokens.' The bound is on the proportion of nontrivial zeros of ζ that are simple and on the critical line, raised from 41.6% to 67.2%. The arXiv paper is Alpöge and Furman, 'More than two thirds of the zeta zeros are simple and on the critical line' (arXiv 2608.13637, v1 13 Aug 2026, v2 19 Aug 2026), whose comments read 'Proof discovered autonomously by Claude (Anthropic); verified and communicated by the listed authors.' The post says: 'We don’t expect that the techniques Claude used will lead to proving the Riemann hypothesis.' This is a neighbouring quantity, not the operator statement.

events.what_happened: OpenAI's openai/math repository contains 'The Quasi-Riemann Hypothesis: A Zero-Free Half-Plane Re(s) > 7/8' (preprint folder dated 30 Sep 2026). Secondary reports (the PDF was not readable through my tool) say it shows that finite-order Hecke L-functions over Q(√−3) and Dirichlet L-functions have no zeros with Re(s) > 7/8, with the pole at s = 1 allowed, and that a separate 5 Oct preprint gives Re(s) > 11/12 for Dirichlet L-functions. An independent GitHub user (tomoto0, not affiliated with OpenAI) rebuilt the accompanying Lean 4 formalization (2,924 modules, 0 errors, standard axioms only); the same report says the Hecke challenge was not built and the heaviest sections were not re-read by hand, and that the method does not prove RH.

events.what_happened: Carl M. Bender, Dorje C. Brody and Markus P. Müller, 'Hamiltonian for the zeros of the Riemann zeta function' (arXiv 1608.03679, first posted 12 Aug 2016; Phys. Rev. Lett. 118, 130201, 2017). A PT-symmetric Hamiltonian whose eigenvalues correspond to the nontrivial zeros if the eigenfunctions satisfy a suitable boundary condition; classical limit 2xp; iH is PT-symmetric with broken PT symmetry, which leaves open that all eigenvalues are real; a heuristic metric-operator construction. States that if the analysis can be made rigorous and shows H is manifestly self-adjoint, 'then this implies that the Riemann hypothesis holds true'. The authors describe the analysis as heuristic. Predates the window.

disputes.summary: Yakaboylu's own versions disagree on simplicity of the nontrivial zeros: the v13 abstract says a rank-one Riesz projector argument 'entails' simplicity, while the v17 text says 'it is an open question whether all nontrivial Riemann zeros are simple' and states the main theorem under that assumption. The record does not explain the change.

Secondary outlets (a crypto news site and a sponsored-content page; neither opened) attribute a proof of the Riemann hypothesis, or a Hilbert–Pólya operator, to OpenAI or GPT-5. OpenAI's own repository contains no such claim: its README mentions the Riemann zeta function only in connection with the zero-free region, and the Anthropic post does not mention the Hilbert–Pólya operator. I treat the secondary attributions as unsupported.

summary: Nothing in the sources resolves the Hilbert–Pólya statement since 26 January 2024. The only in-window paper that asserts a self-adjoint operator with the nontrivial zeros as spectrum, with a construction, is Yakaboylu's arXiv 2408.15135 (first posted 27 Aug 2024; 17 versions; latest 18 Aug 2026). Its v4 body (21 Oct 2024) says the key similarity transformation is postulated rather than constructed; its v9 (23 Apr 2025) asserts the existence for simple zeros; its v13 (18 Nov 2025) ties self-adjointness to a positivity condition W > 0; and its latest text (v17) says self-adjointness 'rests on the positivity Ŵ > 0', which 'already entails ℜ(ρ)=1/2, and so embodies the content of the RH', and treats simplicity as an open question. The predecessor arXiv 2309.00405 (1 Sep 2023; J. Phys. A 2024) predates the window, and its v3 (31 Jan 2024) concedes that the similarity transformation is not well-defined on the Berry–Keating domain. I found no refereeing or published verification of either paper. The one outside critique I found is Feldmann (Dalhousie, Zenodo, 31 Mar 2026), which gives three obstructions; I found no reply from Yakaboylu in the versions I read. Other operator-side claims since 2024 are either self-published or unrefereed proof claims (Bonelli, twice; Tibedo; Aksman; Kulik; Ladjeroud; Tamburini; Bridger's Lean claim; Valamontes et al. in a journal whose refereeing is not documented), an unrefereed but explicitly partial result (Connes–Consani–Moscovici, who call their argument 'tentative' and list two missing steps), or explicitly not proofs (Suo, Zeraoulia and Caceres, Connes 2026, Shi, Jaksch, Liu's negative result on the BBM mechanism). Wikipedia's article still says the conjecture 'has not yet led to a proof of the Riemann hypothesis' and does not mention any work after 2020 in the references I read. For AI: two in-window results credit AI systems but concern neighbouring quantities. Anthropic's post and the Alpöge–Furman arXiv paper (Aug 2026) raise the proportion of zeros that are simple and on the critical line to about two thirds, and the arXiv comments say the proof was 'discovered autonomously by Claude (Anthropic)'; Anthropic's post does not mention the operator. OpenAI's quasi-Riemann manuscripts (folder dated 30 Sep 2026) show a zero-free half-plane Re(s) > 7/8 for Dirichlet and some Hecke L-functions, with the repository crediting 'an internal OpenAI model'; I did not read the manuscript. No operator-side paper in the record credits an AI system, and the operator papers I read (Yakaboylu, Suo, Connes–Consani–Moscovici, Zeraoulia, Tamburini, Liu) disclose none. Several items I could not read (the OpenAI PDF, the Ladjeroud PDF, the Feldmann PDF, the DPG 2026 abstract) are recorded as such. Close call 1: whether Yakaboylu's v17 counts as a construction at all. It asserts an operator and a positivity equivalence, but the operator's self-adjointness is, on the paper's own statement, conditional on a condition equivalent to RH; it is presented as an equivalence, not a proof. Close call 2: the simplicity claim (v13 vs v17). Close call 3: whether Anthropic's and OpenAI's results count as 'related' at all; I record them as neighbouring, since neither mentions a self-adjoint operator.
competing_reading: Read generously, Yakaboylu's v17 is an explicit operator-theoretic reformulation: an operator with the zeros as spectrum exists if and only if a positivity condition holds, and that condition is equivalent to RH. On that reading the record shows a reduction, not a resolution, and the problem stays open. A stricter reader would say the paper asserts the existence of the operator for simple zeros with a construction (v9, v13) and that its conditionality is only a presentation choice; on that reading, the claim covers the simple-zero case, which the bullet does not restrict to, so it would be partial even if correct. A third reading treats the Anthropic and OpenAI results as AI contributions to 'progress' on this problem; they are not, since they concern the proportion of zeros on the line and a zero-free half-plane, not a self-adjoint operator.
what_would_settle_it: A proof that the positivity condition Ŵ > 0 holds, or any unconditional construction of a self-adjoint operator whose spectrum is all nontrivial zeros with multiplicity, checked by specialists in spectral theory; a written reply by Yakaboylu to Feldmann's obstructions; a referee report on the J. Phys. A 2024 version and on any journal submission of arXiv 2408.15135; a Lean formalisation of any operator claim (none found for this problem's operator papers, except the unverified Bridger post); and for the AI attribution, the authors' statement of what the model contributed to the Alpöge–Furman proof and the OpenAI quasi-Riemann manuscript's own disclosure, which I did not read.
